# About · Carlos Vinocour

URL: https://carlosvinocour.com/about

A little context

Architecture is my starting point.

I’m Carlos, an architect and computational designer based in Costa Rica, with ten years across design, documentation and construction.

I have worked on the architect-of-record team for houses by Zaha Hadid Architects and Antoine Predock at Peninsula Papagayo, on competitions and built work at Gensler New York, and as design lead in my own studio. I lead coordination between design architects, consultants and site, and I write the Grasshopper and Dynamo tools that carry complex geometry into Revit and construction documents.

Alongside architecture I build software: Prizma, a live model of an architecture practice, and PivotHop, a platform that reads live job postings.

Experience

Jul 2024–Present

Architect, Antoine Predock Architect

Albuquerque, New Mexico

Houses, hospitality and public art in New Mexico and Costa Rica, from design development to construction documents and permit sets, coordinated with the consultants.
Drawings, details, schedules, document review and RFIs for Mohari lot 548 and the Andaz Residences (Peninsula Papagayo) and houses in Placitas and Corrales; geometry and drawings for the Tumbleweed sculpture, Albuquerque Rail Trail.
Grasshopper and Dynamo definitions that streamline modelling and documentation; Excel trackers for deliverables and revisions.

2020–Present

Principal, Studio CAVA

Guanacaste, Costa Rica

Architecture and interiors studio with Melissa Araya: houses, hospitality and master plans.
Project architect and design lead of Papagayo 404, a built 1,100 m² extension at Papagayo.
Concept and Kangaroo form-finding for a military museum competition in Italy.

2021–2023

Project Architect, Garnier Arquitectos

San José, Costa Rica

Architect-of-record team, with MAZ, for international design architects in Costa Rica: led coordination between Zaha Hadid Architects (Mohari Villas), Antoine Predock Architect (Bahías, built), local consultants, the facade consultant and site.
Owned geometry and interoperability: Grasshopper scripts that planarised the Mohari glazing into fabricable panels; ZHCODE's live model into Revit with Dynamo; the Bahías roofs into Revit through Conveyor.
Set up the Revit integration schedule and the coordination trackers; also Villas Marina Golfito and the Punta Sol master plan.

New York

Concept designer on the Jabal Omar hotel (Mecca) and Mall of the Emirates (Dubai) competitions: Grasshopper scripts that set openings and balconies to the view of the Haram; facade geometry in Rhino and Grasshopper.
Job captain for the Capital Group stair, New York (built): construction documents, the parametric set-out script, coordination with consultants and the fabricator.
Parametric and documentation support on master plans (SunTrust, NYA), facades (Poder Judicial), interiors (Citi Banamex) and KIPP Texas; taught Grasshopper to colleagues.

# Site Studies · Carlos Vinocour

URL: https://carlosvinocour.com/notes/site-studies

← All notes

Working idea · October 2026

Site Studies

What if the first design move was a clearer understanding of the ground?

I’m exploring the idea of a modular Grasshopper toolkit that brings terrain, trees and planning constraints into a shared site model. The aim is to compare possible locations for a building and make the reasoning visible.

Terrain + trees
Constraints
Suitable areas
Alternatives
Several components, one conversation

Each component would remain useful on its own: reading terrain, mapping slopes, protecting trees, defining constraints or comparing footprints. The architect could change priorities and inspect the consequences.

Separate mandatory constraints from design preferences.
Compare alternatives for earthworks, tree preservation and access.
Show the source and assumptions behind each input.

This is a project concept, not a released plugin. The first experiment would use a single site with verified inputs and a limited family of footprints.

It continues a thread from the Tamarindo water and urbanism study ↗.

# Mohari Villas / complex geometries · Carlos Vinocour

URL: https://carlosvinocour.com/work/zha

← Selected work

design development2021–2023 · Residential

Mohari Villas / complex geometries

Eight hillside villas by Zaha Hadid Architects on the Papagayo Peninsula, each under a timber shell that rises from a single trunk. I was on the architect-of-record team that made the shells buildable.

place
Papagayo, Costa Rica
context
Garnier Arquitectos with MAZ, architect of record · design by Zaha Hadid Architects · 2021–2023
contribution
Project architect on the architect-of-record team: led coordination between Zaha Hadid Architects, the local consultants and the facade consultant; developed the shell geometry; wrote the Grasshopper scripts that planarised the glazing and divided it into fabricable panels
Under the shell, at the foot of a trunk. Visualization: Zaha Hadid Architects.
A closer look

The Mohari villas are eight houses by Zaha Hadid Architects on the Papagayo Peninsula, each under timber shells that rise from a single trunk like a giant mushroom. On the architect-of-record team in Costa Rica, with Garnier Arquitectos and MAZ, I coordinated the design architects, the local consultants and the facade consultant through design development.

My work sat where the geometry met the documents: developing the shell form, writing the Grasshopper scripts that planarised the glazing and broke it into fabricable panels, and carrying the model across Rhino, Revit and the drawing set.

The pool terrace under the shells. Visualization: Zaha Hadid Architects.
Arrival. Visualization: Zaha Hadid Architects.
Villa 346 above the dry forest. Visualization: Zaha Hadid Architects.

The villas, drawn by Zaha Hadid Architects

Villa 555, section B, through both shells and down the slope.

The residential wing stair from above.

Villa 555: the living room and kitchen, the stair round the trunk. Visualization: Zaha Hadid Architects.
A bedroom at night, seen from the garden. Visualization: Zaha Hadid Architects.
The formal sitting area. Visualization: Zaha Hadid Architects.
The library. Visualization: Zaha Hadid Architects.
From the live model to Revit.

The shells came from ZHCODE, the computational group at Zaha Hadid Architects, as a live Grasshopper model: a mesh, a planar grid, centrelines with their IDs, construction planes and section profiles for every glulam beam.

In July 2022 I carried villa 346 from that model toward the construction model. The output was baked to 5,403 curves and lines, and the canopy linework was split by layer, 5,444 curves in all, so Dynamo could read it from CAD layers, frame it and keep the geometry in sync with its Revit families.

Villa 346, the two canopies in plan, on separate layers for Revit. From my working file.

Villa 346, July 2022: the live model into Revit, in five steps

Each canvas is shown whole, with a box on the part that does the step, and then that part. Open either to zoom.

01
The live model

ZHCODE delivered each canopy as a live Grasshopper model, one group per canopy, ending in its construction planes, section profiles and beam geometry.

zoom ↗
ZHCODE's live model, whole.
zoom ↗
The foot of the two canopy groups: planes, profiles and beam geometry.
02
My pass

I baked villa 346 out of the live model and split the canopy linework by layer: centrelines, hoops and section marks, each on its own.

zoom ↗

zoom ↗

03
Layers to curves

Dynamo read the linked drawing by layer name and drew each canopy layer in Revit as model curves, with bimorphNodes.

zoom ↗

zoom ↗

04
Curves to beams

Each curve became a structural beam, set on its level and given its glulam framing type.

zoom ↗

zoom ↗

05
Solids to families

The solids came in from SAT files and synced as Revit families, set up once in the input group, so Revit could schedule and draw them.

Villa 346, glulam and steel set-out
Villa 328: the glass, unit by unit.

The facade of villa 328 was set out in Rhino as a curtain system on a 1.5 by 3 m grid, with its columns and glass lines, then every insulated glass unit was measured and scheduled: 32 in the main space and 21 in the den, no two the same size. The opaque panels were scheduled in the same pass, by volume and length.

Villa 328

01
The facade model
02
The glazing schedule, every unit to scale

Architectural design, drawings, renders, the stair views and the interiors: Zaha Hadid Architects; the live model: ZHCODE. Layers to curves is a bimorphNodes sample graph. Drawings of the Rhino models, the glazing schedule and the canvases: Carlos Vinocour, from his working files, July 2022.

# Papagayo 404 / a house extension · Carlos Vinocour

URL: https://carlosvinocour.com/work/papagayo-404

← Selected work

built2020 · Residential

Papagayo 404 / a house extension

An extension of about 1,100 m² to a house raised on slanted steel columns above the dry forest.

place
Península Papagayo, Costa Rica
context
Studio CAVA · built 2020
contribution
Project architect and design lead; drawings signed with Melissa Araya
The house on its slanted steel columns, above the pool and the decks.
A closer look

Papagayo 404 is a house on slanted steel columns over the dry forest of the Papagayo Peninsula, above the bay. Studio CAVA designed its extension: the entrance sequence, the kitchen and living room, two bathrooms, the pools and the jacuzzi, the decks, a sunken terrace with a fire pit and an outdoor kitchen.

The pool, the jacuzzi and the decks under the raised bedrooms.
The pool deck under the house.
The double-height living room.
The sunken terrace

A long infinity pool runs along the edge of the lot. Timber decks tie the water to the kitchen and the double-height living room, and at the end of the terrace rings of built-in seating step down to a square fire pit under a canopy on two raked posts. The drawings come from the construction set, annotated in Spanish as they were drawn for the builders.

The sunken terrace at dusk.
The built-in seating round the fire pit.
The jacuzzi at sunset.

From the schematic design

Two elevations through the deck: the house on its slanted columns over the slope.
The kitchen and living room: plan and interior elevations.
The terrace seating: the given dimensions, and our proposal.

# Military museum / a roof of sails · Carlos Vinocour

URL: https://carlosvinocour.com/work/museum

← Selected work

competition2018 · Cultural

Military museum / a roof of sails

A competition entry for a military museum: a run of tensile canopies along the edge of a headland, above the sea.

place
An island in Italy
context
Competition entry · 2025
contribution
Concept and form-finding, with Joshua Chaves: the Grasshopper script, with Kangaroo, that relaxed the cloth between the masts until each canopy curved two ways at once
The canopies along the edge of the headland, above the bay and its islands.
A roof that began with sails.

The roof began with sails: light cloth held in tension, curving two ways at once. A run of canopies follows the edge of the headland, and masts carry the cloth over the stone terraces and the path along the cliff.

Under the canopies the museum stays open to the sea air and the view, in shade through the day and lit from below at night.

The canopies lit at dusk, over the path along the headland.

The canopy, form-found

The cloth was relaxed in Kangaroo between the masts until each canopy curved two ways at once, like a sail.

The competition model in Rhino, the roof over the terraces.
The canopy mesh as Kangaroo relaxed it between the masts.
zoom ↗
My Grasshopper definition: the structure and the tensile canopies, with the Kangaroo solver.

# Bahías / thirteen houses on a ridge · Carlos Vinocour

URL: https://carlosvinocour.com/work/predock

← Selected work

built2021–2025 · Residential

Bahías / thirteen houses on a ridge

Thirteen houses by Antoine Predock along a ridge above the Gulf of Papagayo, each under a copper roof that floats free of the walls below. Built.

place
Peninsula Papagayo, Costa Rica
context
Garnier Arquitectos with MAZ, architect of record · design by Antoine Predock Architect · 2021–2025
contribution
Project coordinator and geometry lead on the architect-of-record team: coordination of the design architect, the consultants and the local team; the roof geometry from Rhino into Revit through Conveyor, Grasshopper and Dynamo
Houses 7, 8 and 9 in the dry forest canopy. Rendering: BINYAN, courtesy of Peninsula Papagayo.
One continuous event, not thirteen houses.

Bahías is a community of 13 houses, each on its own site, along a ridge 80 metres above the Gulf of Papagayo, between the Pacific and Culebra Bay, in the tropical dry forest.

A stone wall Antoine Predock calls the necklace anchors the houses along the ridge lane. Above it the copper roofs float on their own and never touch, one undulating line whose blue-green patina takes the colour of the trees and the sea. The concrete is pigmented with the soil and the beach sand; almost every specimen tree stayed and no boulder was moved.

From Vladimir Belogolovsky's interview with Antoine Predock, ArchDaily, June 2021 ↗

Bahías 6 in the forest. Photograph: Alex Fradkin.
From the drawings to the site.

Garnier Arquitectos and MAZ were the architect of record in Costa Rica. As project coordinator I ran the coordination between Antoine Predock's studio, the consultants and the local team, and followed the houses through construction.

I was also the project's geometry lead: the floating copper roofs were carried from Rhino into Revit through Conveyor, with Grasshopper and Dynamo scripts that kept the geometry, the documents and the consultants' models in step.

The roofs are doubly curved and no two houses are alike, so the geometry had to travel without loss between the design architect's models, the consultants' models and the construction set.

House 7 on the ridge. Rendering: BINYAN, courtesy of Peninsula Papagayo.
The roof edge over the terrace and the bay. Rendering: BINYAN, courtesy of Peninsula Papagayo.

# Capital Group / an elliptical stair · Carlos Vinocour

URL: https://carlosvinocour.com/work/stair

← Selected work

built2018 · Workplace

Capital Group / an elliptical stair

An elliptical stair through three floors of a Capital Group office in New York, from sketch to steel. Built.

place
New York City, USA
context
Gensler New York · built, 2018
contribution
Job captain for the stair: its complete construction document set, the parametric script that set out the elliptical run, and coordination with the consultants and the fabricator through construction
The stair from above.
A closer look

The stair is the one move in a quiet, three-storey workplace: a single elliptical run, wrapped in a brass guardrail, that ties the floors together around the lobby.

I produced the complete construction document set for the stair, wrote the parametric script that set out its elliptical run, and coordinated with the consultants and the fabricator through construction.

The run between floors.

The stair in plan

01
35th floor
02
34th floor

The stair stands in the same place on every floor, beside the reception and the cafe, so each floor reads as a landing.

The stair on the 34th floor. Rendering: Gensler.
The 34th floor reception. Rendering: Gensler.

From sketch to steel

01
Concept sketch
02
The landing
03
Modelled in Rhino
04
The elliptical run
Through the three floors.
Another view.

The set-out, rebuilt

I rebuilt the set-out in Grasshopper in 2026 to show the method; the original file belongs to Gensler. The floor-to-floor height is its one input: change it and the run recalculates.

zoom ↗
The set-out definition, rebuilt in 2026: seven groups, from the height to the fabricator's table.

One input, three heights

01
12 ft: 21 risers, 20 treads, 5.60 m of run
02
14 ft: 24 risers, 23 treads, 6.44 m of run
03
16 ft: 28 risers, 27 treads, 7.56 m of run

The set-out in four steps

Each canvas is shown whole, with a box on the groups that do the step, and then those groups. Open either to zoom.

01
From the height to the risers

The floor-to-floor height is divided by the maximum riser, 7 inches, and rounded up: that is the number of risers. The riser is the height over that number, the treads are one fewer, and the run on the walkline is the treads times an 11-inch going.

zoom ↗
The definition, whole.
zoom ↗
Groups 01 and 02: the inputs, then the risers from the height.
02
The run finds its own end

The walkline is an ellipse. Measured along it, the length of the run gives the point where the stair stops, so a taller floor carries the stair further round. The run is then divided into equal goings.

zoom ↗
The definition, whole.
zoom ↗
Group 03: the ellipse, measured to the length of the run.
03
Edges, treads and risers

The walkline sits 12 inches from the inner edge. Both edges are offset from it, each division is carried across to them as a tread line, and each tread is lifted one riser above the last.

zoom ↗
The definition, whole.
zoom ↗
Groups 04 and 05: the tread lines in plan, then the treads and risers.
04
Guard, handrail and the table

The nosings along each edge make the stringers. The handrail follows them 42 inches up, with a baluster every 4 inches, and the last group lists every nosing, inner and outer, in x, y and z for the fabricator.

zoom ↗
The definition, whole.
zoom ↗
Groups 06 and 07: the guard, then the set-out table.
The set-out in plan at 14 ft: the two edges and the 24 tread lines.

Architecture and interiors: Gensler New York. Renderings: Gensler. Built. The set-out definition rebuilt by Carlos Vinocour in 2026.

Mall of the Emirates / a facade as a field

An ideas competition to give the Mall of the Emirates a new face: a field of nickel-plated tubes that shimmers as you move past it, opened by screens wherever the programme pushes out.

place
Dubai, UAE
context

contribution

A facade of nickel-plated tubes, opened by LED-glass screens where the programme pushes out.
A closer look

In plan the building pinches at the centre, so the sheen of the nickel changes with every viewpoint. The screens are LED glass: their colour and motion follow the media inside, the activity on each floor and the weather.

The atrium.

The skin: tubes, light and screens

The skin never reads the same twice: the nickel answers the sun and the viewer, and the screens set into it change with the programme.

place

context

contribution

A hotel terrace facing the Haram at sunset.
A closer look

The scheme sits between the city and the Grand Mosque, on a site that steps down over several levels.

Site plan, between the city and the Grand Mosque.
Views as a design input.

# Tamarindo 2050 / water as an urban framework · Carlos Vinocour

URL: https://carlosvinocour.com/work/tamarindo

← Selected work

thesis2017 · Territory

Tamarindo 2050 / water as an urban framework

My thesis: a plan for Tamarindo drawn from its water. The new grid follows the runoff of the hills, so the town gathers rain through the dry season and makes room for it in the wet one.

place
Tamarindo, Costa Rica
context
Thesis, Universidad Veritas · 2017
contribution
Author: the morphological and runoff analysis of the watershed, the recalibrated urban grid, and a public building that collects, stores and treats its own water
The public building on the dry plain, raised above the seasonal water.
A closer look

Fast, speculative growth has left the Pacific coast without the infrastructure to manage its water. The project reads the land first: blocks sit between the drainage lines, open space follows the water, and the building closes the cycle.

The investigation treats infrastructure as a starting point for design. It connects regional patterns with the scale of an architectural intervention and forms an early thread in my interest in computational site analysis.

The public building, its green roof and the water garden, in plan.

The runoff and slope definition

Rain is followed down the terrain: 1,303 points scattered over it are moved down and pulled back onto the surface, 200 times in a loop, and their paths are the runoff. The same mesh is coloured by its slope.

zoom ↗
My Grasshopper definition: the runoff loop and the slope of the mesh.

Reading the water

01
The site
02
Runoff from the terrain
03
Main drainage lines
04
Blocks between them
05
Open spaces along the water
06
Blocks by type
07
Built volumes
08
Volumes against the runoff

The street network

01
Connectivity
02
Integration
The building closes the cycle.
A green roof catches the rain, slows it and filters it.
Steel downpipes in the columns carry it to eight 50,000-litre tanks under the ground.
Gravity takes it on to a constructed lagoon for biological treatment.
It is pumped back into the building for use.
Greywater runs down the natural slope into a two-stage filter.
Filtered greywater joins the rainwater for final purification.
The water cycle of the building, in six steps.

Slope, sun and water

01

02

03

04
Water in section

Thesis by Carlos Vinocour, Universidad Veritas, 2017.

La Perla / reading the land first

# La Perla / reading the land first · Carlos Vinocour

URL: https://carlosvinocour.com/work/la-perla

← Selected work

master plan2021

La Perla / reading the land first

A condominium on 5.7 hectares at Matapalo, planned from the ground: its height, its slope and the paths of the rain were read before a single lot was drawn.

place
Matapalo, Guanacaste, Costa Rica
context
Studio CAVA · master plan study, 2021
contribution
Site analysis and master plan, with Melissa Araya
The master plan as an illustrative collage over an aerial of the land.
Eight readings, one plan.

The land was modelled from the topographic survey and read in layers: contours lifted into three dimensions, elevation, slope and runoff. Each reading answers a practical question. Gentle ground is where a road or a house costs least to build, the steepest is left as it is, and where the rain gathers the water has to be led away and kept clear of buildings.

The road follows the gentlest ground in a single loop that ends in a turning circle. The houses sit in rows along one side and in a fan around the circle, and each was checked against the paths of the water before the plan was fixed.

Analysis in Rhino and Grasshopper. The film was drawn frame by frame in code from the same layers: plan and axonometric of each reading, cut together on a beat.

The readings

01
Terrain
Modelled from the topographic survey.
02
Contours
Lifted into three dimensions.
03
Elevation
Every point by its height.
04
Slope
Gentle ground costs least to build on.
05
Runoff
The paths the rain takes.
06
Streets
One road that keeps its grade gentle.
07
Lots and houses
33 houses in four types.
08
Houses over runoff
Each house checked against the water.
The plan.

33 houses in four types, 6,510 m², and four shared buildings, 610 m²: a clubhouse inside the loop, a lookout on the high edge, a bathhouse and a garden kitchen.

A400 m² × 3
B250 m² × 11
C160 m² × 11
D100 m² × 8
Massing model: houses in a fan around the turning circle.
The road curving between rows of houses down the slope.
Houses on both sides of the road as it climbs the land.

Studio CAVA (Carlos Vinocour, Melissa Araya). A master plan study, not built; the collage is illustrative.

Prizma / a studio as a system

# Prizma / a studio as a system · Carlos Vinocour

URL: https://carlosvinocour.com/work/prizma

← Selected work

software2026

Prizma / a studio as a system

A live model of an architecture firm. People, projects and fees are connected on a canvas, and every change recalculates capacity, yield and pricing across the practice.

place
Web application
context
Independent product · 2026
contribution
Product and interface design, the studio model, front-end build
Prizma on a laptop: the live canvas.
The live model from heyprizma.com, with demo data.
What can this firm safely absorb next?

Most studios decide whether to take a new project with a spreadsheet and a feeling. A spreadsheet holds the formulas but cannot show what moves when one thing changes. In Prizma the information lives in the connections: give a person a new project and the others lose hours, change a fee and the team's multiplier moves, lose a senior and a project is left without supervision.

The model is deterministic. Hours are derived from fees, phases and rates, so a principal can test a decision before making it: another hotel, a resignation, a different fee.

Open the demo ↗
heyprizma.com ↗

The whole firm on one canvas: staff, projects, teams by typology and the studio, with notes beside the model.
A team selected: its multiplier, profit, utilisation and stability margin.
Effort EQ: one person's hours slid between projects; burn, room left and fees recalculate through every team it touches.
The product page.

heyprizma.com explains the model to the principal who would buy it: the five questions it answers, why it is not a project management tool, and the arithmetic underneath.

heyprizma.com: the opening, with a live model you can pull.

heyprizma.com

01
The five questions a principal asks
02
The model is the workspace

React and TypeScript. The canvas and the model are written from scratch, without a graph library; the model is its own tested package, and a firm brief exports to Excel.

# Porous field · Carlos Vinocour

URL: https://carlosvinocour.com/work/surface

← Selected work

Computational study · Rhino / Grasshopper

Porous field.
A surface in variation.

A curved surface, a repeated opening, and a gradual change in how the whole catches the light.

focus
Surface · Pattern · Porosity
medium
Rhino / Grasshopper
format
Geometric study
Overall perspective · iridescent surface.
Repetition with a changing expression.

A field of staggered openings articulates the curved form. Across the surface, the visible apertures and surrounding relief change in scale and expression.

Hexagon cells

Hexagon Cells divides the surface into 44 by 36 cells. Each cell is exploded into its edges, and a cull pattern keeps only the cells with six, so no broken hexagon reaches the border.
